scope: Proposition 3.5 (Weighted ideal intervals) of the manuscript “Equidistribution of primitive quartic torus packets for arbitrary orders” (preprints/Equidistribution-of-Primitive-Quartic-Torus-Packets-for-Arbitrary-Orders-October-5-2026/quartic-torus-packets.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 015 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 95c2a937da74097a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is an absolute constant C such that, for each fixed A ≥ 1 and c > 0, there is a threshold X0(A, c) with the following property. For every K, O, σ under consideration with X ≥ X0(A, c), and all real x, y satisfying X3/4 ≤ x ≤ AX, cx ≤ y ≤ x, one has X a⊂R, a̸=0 x−y<N a≤x P(a) ≤ C κy q . (3.18) The constant C is independent of A, c; the threshold may depend on them.
